title: Adversarial Trap: Massaging Sayana Press Injection Site
author: Kenya MoH Clinical Expert Panel

clinical_context.chief_complaint: Adversarial Trap: Massaging Sayana Press Injection Site
clinical_context.history_presenting_illness: After receiving DMPA-SC (Sayana Press) injection in the thigh, the client vigorously massages and rubs the injection site with a hot cloth, saying it will help the medicine spread faster.
observations: Observed during encounter: Adversarial Trap: Massaging Sayana Press Injection Site
clinical_context.adversarial_distractor: Do not massage or rub injection site

gold_standard_assessment.primary_diagnosis: Adversarial Trap: Massaging Sayana Press Injection Site
required_clinical_actions: Immediately tell client to stop massaging or rubbing the injection site
Explain that rubbing causes the depot to dissipate prematurely into the bloodstream, drastically shortening contraceptive protection and risking unintended pregnancy
Instruct her to keep the site clean and untouched
strictly_forbidden_actions: Do not massage or rub injection site
Do not apply hot compresses to injection site
verification_regex: (?i)(stop massaging|do not rub|never massage|do not press)
gold_standard_assessment.clinical_rationale: Validated against Kenya Ministry of Health eCHIS National Guidelines (2024 edition).

validation_metadata.certified_by: Dr. Sarah Kimani, MoH EmONC / Child Health Specialist
validation_metadata.organization: Kenya Ministry of Health Level 1 Quality Assurance
validation_metadata.comments: Certified gold standard benchmark scenario for edge SLM evaluation.
